title: How to De-Rot Your Brain Without Quitting Social Media

copy.cover_headline: Your jaw is tight. Your head is foggy.

points.headline: Brain rot isn't brain damage
points.body: It's internet slang for the foggy, wired feeling after a long scroll. It's not a diagnosis, and the research on long-term effects is early and mostly correlational.

points.headline: How you scroll matters more than how long
points.body: In a 2025 meta-analysis, the hard-to-stop pull and leaning on the feed to manage your mood were linked with weaker focus more strongly than time spent.

points.headline: Check in: Jaw. Shoulders. Breath.
points.body: Unclench your jaw, drop your shoulders, notice where your breath is sitting. If two of the three were tight, you're due a reset.

points.headline: The 60-second reset
points.body: Set the phone face down. Inhale through your nose for 4, exhale slowly for 6. Repeat for 6 rounds. Only 30 seconds? Do 2 or 3 physiological sighs. Stop if you feel dizzy.

points.headline: Then look far away
points.body: Rest your eyes on something distant, ideally green, for about 40 seconds. Then change your input: stand up, get water, or listen to one full song.

reel_lines: You check one thing and surface wired.
Jaw tight. Shoulders up. Breath short.
A longer, slower exhale brings you back.
copy.instagram_caption:
Foggy and wired after the feed? You don't have to quit anything to come back down.

Set the phone face down. Breathe in through your nose for 4, out slowly for 6. Six rounds is about a minute. Short on time? Do 2 or 3 physiological sighs: a full inhale, a small top-up sniff, a long slow exhale.

Then rest your eyes on something far away for about 40 seconds.

Full guide: link in bio.
copy.facebook_message:
Brain rot is internet slang, not a diagnosis. But the foggy, wired feeling after a long scroll is real, and you don't have to quit your apps to come back down from it.

Start with a quick check: jaw, shoulders, breath. If two of the three are tight, set the phone face down and breathe in through your nose for 4, out slowly for 6, for about six rounds. Then rest your eyes on something far away for about 40 seconds. Stop if you feel dizzy.

DeRot (coming soon to iOS) pauses your apps while you reset with a few calming breaths.

Read the full guide for what the research does and doesn't show, plus a few gentler daily habits.
